title: indirection-handles-and-background-defragmentation-for-kv-pool
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: KV cache allocation is suffering from medium-to-high fragmentation after extended traffic with varied sequence lengths and model mixes. Fragmentation increases GPU memory pressure, forcing us to evict warm KV entries during continuous batching bursts and raising tail latency. Existing allocators leak small holes and relocations are expensive when we attempt in-place compaction, which interferes with latency SLOs.

Proposal summary: Introduce a two-layer memory abstraction for the GPU KV cache: 1) stable indirection handles (4- or 8-byte CPU-pinned indices) that remain constant while entries move, and 2) a set of typed arenas pooled by allocation size-class and model-affinity. A background defragmenter uses an opportunistic, copy-based compaction technique that migrates live entries to a fresh arena using asynchronous CUDA copies on a low-priority stream. The indirection table is updated atomically (via double-buffered pointer flips with version stamps) so active inference threads never dereference invalid raw GPU addresses.

Goals: reduce fragmentation by 60% for mixed-length workloads, avoid client-visible pauses during live compaction, preserve continuous batching throughput, and lower eviction-induced reruns by 40% in our synthetic replay tests.
updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed. Prototype indirection table in CPU-pinned memory and sample migrator using CUDA memcpyAsync. Observed stable handles reduce lock contention during relocation.
2026-02-20: Design review with runtime and batching teams. Decided to use size-class arenas (powers-of-two up to 1MB) and a small fast-path for frequent small KV keys (<=512B).
2026-02-28: Implemented indirection handle API and unit tests. Added handle version stamp to detect stale handles returned to clients after eviction.

2026-03-05: Integration test with continuous batching harness. Verified no 99th-percentile latency spikes during small-scale compaction runs when compaction limited to <2% of allocator capacity per-second.
2026-03-12: PR opened (see links). Requested perf review and QA for larger replay workloads.
acceptance_criteria: No client-visible pointer invalidation: inference requests using existing handles do not crash or return corruption during background compaction.
Fragmentation metric (free-run length distribution) reduced by >=60% on mixed-model replay compared to current allocator baseline.
End-to-end throughput for continuous batching workloads is within 5% of baseline when compaction runs at planned throttle rates.
Eviction rate due to out-of-memory during 24h mixed replay reduced by >=40%.
Automated e2e test that simulates heavy model churn and validates handle versioning and eviction semantics.
milestones: M1: API & indirection table design doc (done) - 2026-02-14
M2: Core allocator arenas + size-class allocator implemented - 2026-02-26
M3: Background migrator + atomic indirection swap - 2026-03-04
M4: Integration with continuous batching harness and perf tests - 2026-03-10
M5: Rollout to canary fleet and metrics validation - 2026-03-22
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Atomic swap of indirection table could become a contention hotspot. Mitigation: sharded indirection table keyed by model-id and batch-slice to limit atomic region size.

Risk: Background memcpy increases PCIe/GPU bandwidth usage and may affect inference. Mitigation: throttle migrator to low-priority CUDA stream and apply adaptive rate limit based on real-time latency signals.
Risk: Versioned handles add CPU pinned memory overhead. Mitigation: compress handle table entries and use 32-bit indices where possible; track memory usage in console.
Risk: Edge-case stale handles from long-running batches. Mitigation: incorporate handle expiration and explicit eviction callbacks to callers; fallback to re-fetch on miss.
qa_plan: Unit tests for handle creation, lookup, and stale-detection.
Integration test: replay mixed-length workload for 24h in staging with compaction enabled and disabled to collect delta metrics.
Chaos test: randomly pause migrator and validate no memory corruption or crashes.
Performance regression tests against continuous-batching harness with 0/1/2 compaction worker counts.
implementation_notes: Keep indirection table in CPU-pinned memory to allow atomic updates without device syncs for common cases.
Use double-buffering for arena metadata updates: prepare new mapping, publish pointer flip, then lazily reclaim old blocks.
Expose throttling knobs via runtime config and Console so SRE can tune per-deployment.
Add telemetry: per-arena fragmentation histogram, migrator bandwidth, compaction latency, and handle-stale counters.
